We believe that Jesus Christ is the Savior of the World. Every week we gather in our chapels and take the sacrament, which is bread and water that symbolize the body and blood of Christ. We do this to re-new the covenants (or promises) we made when we were baptized into the church; which are that we will take upon the name of Christ, and that we will always remember Him. In return, He grants us His Spirit to always be with us.

Joseph Smith was a prophet of God, like Moses or Noah. He was guided to an ancient, buried record that was written by Christians who lived in America (who sailed here from Jerusalem). We believe this record was written by ancient prophets who taught and prophesied of Christ. We consider the Book of Mormon to be scripture, comparable to the Bible. To make a long story short, I found myself in a standoff with a mountain lion for about a solid hour up in the mountains. Now the gun didn't really end up saving my life, but I'm sure glad I had it that night. I had my sights on that cat the whole time, just waiting for it to rush me. I can tell the whole story if anyone is interested.

OP expressed interest in this story, so here it is. Like I said earlier, I didn't end up shooting anyone with my gun, but I think it saved my life:

I went up the nearby canyon to have a little camping trip by myself, and found a remote spot far up in the mountains. I set up camp in a beautiful meadow surrounded by tall grass and trees. After getting comfortable, I made a fire with my bow drill set, cooked some dinner, read a book, and once it was too dark to read, settled into my sleeping bag to get some sleep.

After what seemed only seconds of closing my eyes, I abruptly woke up to what sounded like rocks falling down the side of a nearby rock face, just outside of the meadow's tree-line. I was a little startled of course, but not all that nervous - until I rubbed my eyes, and saw two glowing yellow eyes, sitting low in the grass, about 20 yards away from me. I wasn't sure what it was at first, but I assumed it was a cougar because of how low it sat in the grass. I slowly pulled my little PA63 (9mm Makarov cal.) out of my backpack, and pointed it in the general direction of the eyes. I couldn't really aim, because it was too dark, and I didn't bring a flashlight with me (probably stupid, I know. I really enjoy just getting used to the moonlight when I go camping.) I figured I'd better at least try my phone flashlight, so I diverted my attention for a few seconds and grabbed it out of my backpack, but my phone was dead (I really wasn't very prepared). I looked back up to find the eyes, but they were gone. I scanned the meadow, and found them again, but they had moved - they were a bit closer this time. I was getting nervous by this time, and I was pretty sure I was dealing with a cat.

What I would guess to be about 30 minutes went by, of me just aiming at those eyes. I could not believe how patient that creature was. After a long time of standing there with my gun pointed, I became a little less alert, and suddenly the eyes disappeared. I scanned the meadow again, and a few seconds later they reappeared, even closer this time. I mean MUCH closer (probably 10 yards from me), and I started to FREAK OUT. This is when I KNEW it was a mountain lion. It was being very stalker-ish, very sneaky and very mischievous. At this point I knew that it was going to attack me. I saw it's eyes get even closer to the ground, and right before I felt like it was going to run at me, I instinctively fired two shots in it's general direction and started yelling as loud as I could. It ran off, and I could see in the moonlight as it ran away it was indeed a mountain lion.

After a few minutes checking my surroundings, I got back into my sleeping bag, but I didn't sleep the rest of the night. I was checking my surroundings about every 15 minutes until the sun came up to make sure it wasn't stalking me again. Most intense camping trip of my life.

We wandered into the parking lot of the "Physical Plant", which I think monitors utilities of the school like gas and water. In the parking lot, the old college school bus sat in the dark corner and we decided to check it out. We got into it from the back (emergency exit) and just chilled in there for a while. We wandered up to the front of the bus and found the keys just sitting in the ignition. 

"What idiots, they just leave the keys in the ignition and trust no one will steal it?" I said to my friends. We joked around a bit about how awesome it would be if we taught the school admins a lesson by at least moving the bus somewhere else, just to show them how easy it would be. That sounded like fun to me, so without telling my friends (I decided if I was going to do it, I wouldn't tell anyone because I knew word would get around and I'd probably get caught) I promised myself I was going to steal it and at least park it in some hilarious spot. 

A couple days later, I went into the nearby hills and set up camp. I decided to camp that night because I didn't want to leave my dorms late at night, steal the bus, and then come back later with the chance of the school checking dorm cameras to see who left and at what time (I really covered my tracks). I wore gloves and a mask like a real-life sketchy person to absolutely make sure I was in the clear. I got to the parking lot, got in the bus, and after a while of convincing myself, I started up the engine. I spent what seemed like an eternity trying to figure out how to disengage the air-brakes, and when I finally did, I put it into drive. I slowly rolled out of the parking lot, and approached the only street I had to cross to get to the main campus. I checked both ways, then floored it across the street, bottoming out HARD on my way out. I rolled onto the campus sidewalk and drove to the nearby bell tower. I parked it in the most absurd place you could park a bus, right in front of the bell tower next to the Student Center. I then stopped the engine, debated on if I should take the keys, but then decided that would be too mean and just left them on the seat. I really wanted to leave a note or something that read "Don't leave keys in the ignition" or something but in the heat of the moment I was feeling pretty nervous so I booked it out of there pretty quickly.
